answers.note: One formation is within renewal at its step and consuming over the run. It refutes RenewingAt (step) → RenewingIn (run), and RenewingAt → not ConsumingIn; and, since Widens l web.level contradicts Includes web.level l, it shows E22 fails with the stepwise class in place of the run class, for this one event (RenewingAt is given at step 0 only, not at every step). The statement itself places CONSUMING over the run together with NARROWS of the same formation's part: one case, no general law. The docstring's 'the run class is the one that tells the part's place' is a reading across this case and E22, more than the statement.

answers.note: Only one listed side is named, and it stands denied. The case: an active event that is not undermining, whose part still narrows what can form and loses something with significance. It refutes 'an event that is not undermining (a living event) belongs to a part that keeps what can form', and so the converse of E19 for this event: levels exceeded with no undermining at that event. The denial is of the event at step 0 only; the statement does not deny undermining at later steps. With E23 (same built web): the same event is within renewal at its step, not undermining at its step, and its formation consumes over the run. I did not open Significance.lean.
